questions.question: The S segment of Uukuniemi virus (family Phenuiviridae) utilizes an ambisense coding strategy. Which statement correctly describes the transcription strategy of this viral RNA segment?
options: The viral nucleoprotein (N) mRNA is transcribed directly from the genomic RNA, whereas the non-structural protein (NSs) mRNA is transcribed from the antigenomic replicative intermediate.
Both N and NSs proteins are transcribed from a single, full-length bicistronic mRNA that undergoes internal ribosome entry site (IRES)-mediated translation.
The S segment contains a double-stranded RNA core where positive-sense strands code for N and negative-sense strands code for NSs.
The viral envelope glycoproteins are encoded in the genomic orientation, while the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase is encoded in the antigenomic orientation.

questions.question: Which biological property fundamentally distinguishes virophages (such as the Sputnik virophage) from typical satellite viruses?
options: Virophages integrate into host bacterial genomes as prophages, whereas satellite viruses cannot integrate.
Virophages can replicate in host cells autonomously without requiring co-infection by a helper virus.
Virophages directly parasitize the viral replication factory of a giant helper virus, impairing its replication efficiency and causing virion morphogenesis defects.
Virophages possess a single-stranded RNA genome, whereas all satellite viruses possess double-stranded DNA genomes.

questions.question: During West Nile virus entry into a host cell, which viral structural protein mediates attachment to cell surface receptors and undergoes low-pH-induced conformational changes within endosomes to trigger membrane fusion?
options: Capsid (C) protein
Envelope (E) glycoprotein
Membrane (M) protein
Non-structural protein 1 (NS1)

questions.question: Xenotropic endogenous retroviruses (such as xenotropic murine leukemia viruses) are characterized by their unique host range restriction. Which statement accurately describes a xenotropic virus?
options: It replicates exclusively in insect vectors without causing pathology in mammalian hosts.
It integrates into host genomes without utilizing a viral reverse transcriptase.
It replicates only in plant cells via mechanical vector transmission.
It can infect and replicate in cells of foreign host species, but cannot infect cells of the native host species of origin.

questions.question: During congenital Zika virus infection, severe microcephaly and cortical thinning are primarily caused by viral tropism for and viral-induced apoptosis of which cell population in the developing fetal brain?
options: Oligodendrocytes responsible for central nervous system myelination
Mature cerebellar Purkinje cells
Neural progenitor cells (NPCs)
Meningeal mesothelial cells
